about: Planted bugs. Each one breaks one guard, and the named property must fail. Spec mutations edit spec/McpCall.tla and run TLC on MCMcpCall.cfg, once with only the named property and once with all of it. Code mutations edit a copy of src/core/mcp_host/mcp_call.zig, rebuild the harness from it, and run both driver directions. Each find string must occur exactly once.

spec.breaks: A revoked token is still accepted: only a forged one is refused.
A client of another protocol version is admitted.
The capacity check is off by one.
Load is checked before the token, so a client without one learns the bridge is busy.
An admission does not advance the next id, so ids repeat.
A late allow for a withdrawn prompt still runs the call.
A duplicated allow runs the call again.
Letting go of work leaves a running call running.
A subagent's end leaves its prompts and calls running.
Stopping the session keeps its tokens.
A result whose client left is dropped without a log.
A reply reports success whatever the call's outcome.
A subagent's call runs with the session's access.
A duplicated call end writes a second reply.
A disconnect frees the slot while the prompt or call it started still runs.
spec.find: THEN /\ entries' = {IF e.id = i THEN Abandon(e) ELSE e : e \in entries}

spec.breaks: A new process continues the old one's ids.
An admission takes an id past the next one.
A withdrawn prompt's answer never frees its slot.

code.breaks: While the bridge is open, any token is admitted, as the session.
code.replace: const owner: ?OwnerId = if (state.open) OwnerId.main else ownerOf(state, token);
